doc.summary: ShortcutManager is a singleton class that manages global keyboard shortcuts.
doc.details:
The ShortcutManager provides centralized access to system-wide keyboard shortcut registration and handling. It follows the singleton pattern to ensure there's only one instance managing all shortcuts throughout the application lifetime.

Key features:
- Singleton pattern ensures centralized shortcut management
- Event-driven architecture for shortcut activation notifications
- Cross-platform shortcut registration and monitoring
- Thread-safe access to the singleton instance
- Automatic cleanup of resources on destruction
- Support for both global and application-local shortcuts

notes.text:
Platform availability:
- macOS: ✅ Carbon ordinary global hotkeys, with activation/release events. Media keys use a Quartz event tap for global scope and AppKit monitoring for application scope. Global taps require OS authorization and may be restricted by sandbox policy; permission loss unregisters affected global shortcuts. Application media monitoring requires AppKit dispatch but no global tap; app deactivation releases held application media keys.
- Windows: ✅ Win32 global hotkeys; activation events only.
- Linux: ⚠️ X11 registration, or asynchronous Wayland GlobalShortcuts Portal registration through RequestRegistration. Portal support requires a desktop provider and valid application identity; the user controls the final binding.
- Android: ❌ Native shortcut registration is not implemented.
- iOS: ❌ Native shortcut registration is not implemented.
- OpenHarmony: ⚠️ API 14+ public NDK global hotkeys, with Ctrl/Alt/Shift modifiers and an active main dispatcher. Meta/Fn/lock modifiers, release events are not implemented. Application scope uses a mounted companion NativeShortcutHost forwarding normal component key events, without reserving global hotkeys. It requires an initialized UI host and at least one attached key host; only the focused host receives unconsumed input. Global SDK conflicts fail registration. IsAvailable checks global availability by briefly probing native reservations; a competing application may still race a later Register call.
This class is thread-safe for singleton access and shortcut operations.
Shortcut instances should be created and managed through this manager.

notes.text:
Accelerator format follows Electron-style conventions:
- Modifiers: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Cmd (macOS), Super (Linux), Meta
- Keys: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F12, Space, Tab, Enter, Escape, etc.
- macOS media: MediaPlayPause, MediaNextTrack, MediaPreviousTrack, MediaFastForward, MediaRewind, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, VolumeMute, BrightnessUp, BrightnessDown, Eject. NativeMediaKey<N> denotes an explicit macOS NX auxiliary-control code, distinct from Carbon NativeKey<N>. Apple FAST/REWIND and NEXT/PREVIOUS are canonical aliases. One accelerator string identifies one registration; distinct named and numeric aliases can be used to register global and app scopes.
- Examples: "Ctrl+C", "Cmd+Shift+4", "Alt+F4", "Ctrl+Alt+Delete"

doc.summary: Requests registration without waiting for interactive approval.
doc.details: Subscribe before requesting. A nonzero return value identifies this request and its eventual ShortcutRegisteredEvent or ShortcutRegistrationFailedEvent. The shortcut is available through Get only after successful registration. Completion may occur before this method returns; listeners must retain the event's ID rather than assume the caller has already stored the return value.

params.name: registration_key
params.text: Stable, nonempty application-defined action key. Reuse it across launches; description remains human-readable display text.

doc.returns: A nonzero request/shortcut ID if accepted, or 0 for invalid options, an unsupported immediate global backend, or an accelerator/key already pending or active. Deferred providers report unavailable services through the failure event, without synchronously contacting the desktop in this call. Rejected requests emit no completion event. Accepted requests complete once, including cancellation, and failure events always carry this request's ID.

notes.text:
Platform availability:
- macOS: ✅ Immediate Carbon/media registration; same permission and scope requirements as Register. Completion uses shortcut events.
- Windows: ✅ Win32 registration; completion uses shortcut events.
- Linux: ⚠️ X11 registration or asynchronous Wayland Portal approval. Requires a GlobalShortcuts desktop provider. A portal accelerator is a preference; GetTriggerDescription reports the desktop's binding label. Unregister stops the session but does not erase the desktop's saved binding configuration.
- Android: ❌ Global requests return 0; application registration is unsupported.
- iOS: ❌ Global requests return 0; application registration is unsupported.
- OpenHarmony: ⚠️ Same host and scope requirements as Register.

doc.summary: Cancels pending requests belonging to an application-defined key namespace.
doc.details: Useful after an interpreter or Flutter isolate restarts while the native manager survives. Active shortcuts present before this call are unaffected.
